assessment.nobel_worthiness: A clear physical principle (ionic current blockade by a single polymer threading a nanoscale pore) turned into a genuinely new capability: label-free, long-read, single-molecule sequencing of DNA and RNA. It sits where physics, chemistry and biology meet, and the generative potential is large (portable sequencing, direct RNA and modification reading, protein sensing).
assessment.attribution: Kasianowicz, Brandin, Branton and Deamer showed polynucleotide translocation through alpha-hemolysin in 1996; Deamer and Akeson pursued sequencing and enzyme-controlled ratcheting; Bayley engineered pores and adapters. The credit is spread over more than three people, so any trio omits someone decisive. I would separate the original discovery from later engineering, which favors Kasianowicz, Deamer and Akeson, but this is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: the technology is commercial, used widely, and independently confirmed across many laboratories. Recognition is timely and long overdue by physical-principle standards.
uncertainties: Whether Bayley's pore engineering, rather than the original translocation demonstration, is the decisive step.
I am not certain which of Branton and Bayley are living and eligible; this affects the feasible trio.
Whether the committee sees this as chemistry rather than biophysics or instrumentation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskites reached photovoltaic efficiencies near those of silicon within about a decade, with long carrier diffusion lengths and defect tolerance that remain a rich physical problem. This is a striking example of a new materials class approaching fundamental limits and opening new device capabilities, including tandem cells.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka first used perovskites as sensitizers (2009); Park and Snaith, with Seok and others, transformed them into efficient solid-state absorbers (2012); Grätzel and Kanatzidis are also credited. Six credited names make a trio hard, and the priority of Miyasaka versus the 2012 solid-state breakthroughs needs careful treatment.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent replication and rapid, well-documented efficiency growth. Long-term operational stability, toxicity and scale-up are not fully settled, so some of the impact may still be ahead.
uncertainties: Stability and commercial deployment remain unproven at scale.
Fair allocation among six credited people.
Overlap with the dye-sensitized solar cell lineage and Grätzel's role.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Visible-light photoredox catalysis uses well-understood excited-state electron transfer to enable radical chemistry under mild conditions, and has changed how synthetic and medicinal chemists build bonds. The principle is clean and the generative breadth is very large.
assessment.attribution: Yoon, Stephenson and Nicewicz independently reported the early synthetic applications of 2008-2011; MacMillan's contribution is the most visible but he is already a laureate (2021, organocatalysis), which complicates allocation. König, Fukuzumi and Melchiorre made important related contributions.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely adopted in academia and industry, with extensive independent confirmation. Timely.
uncertainties: The relationship to MacMillan's 2021 prize may weigh against recognition.
Earlier precedents in photochemistry (Kellogg, Fukuzumi, Deronzier) complicate the claim of originality.
Seven credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Induced proximity to hijack the ubiquitin-proteasome system turns degradation into a programmable therapeutic modality and expands the druggable proteome. It has strong generative potential, though the underlying biophysics of ternary complex cooperativity is only partly quantified.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies conceived the PROTAC concept; Ciulli contributed VHL ligands and mechanistic work; Handa and Ito identified cereblon as the thalidomide target, a distinct discovery that explains molecular glue degraders. The compound discovery may need different recognition for its parts.
assessment.maturity: Clinical validation is advancing (several compounds in late-stage trials) but no approvals of PROTACs are firmly established, which suggests recognition may be slightly early.
uncertainties: Whether clinical results are sufficient for timing.
How to credit the cereblon and molecular glue strand versus the PROTAC concept.
Eight credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The idea that cells organize biochemistry through liquid-liquid phase separation brings polymer physics and thermodynamics into cell biology and has reshaped thinking about condensates. It is conceptually broad, but its status as chemistry rather than cell biology and physics is debatable.
assessment.attribution: Brangwynne and Hyman demonstrated liquid-like P granules (2009); Rosen showed phase separation of multivalent signaling proteins (2012); Pappu and Mittag contributed physical and sequence-grammar understanding. A fair trio is plausible but contested.
assessment.maturity: The concept is widely confirmed, but debate persists about the physiological relevance of many in vitro condensates and about quantitative evidence in cells. Possibly early.
uncertainties: Controversy over in vivo relevance versus in vitro droplets.
Fit with the chemistry prize remit.
Allocation among five credited people.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Resolving the bond structure of individual molecules with CO-functionalized tips is a conceptually clean, quantitative physical result that yields direct chemical information, including on-surface reaction products, and has been influential in surface chemistry and nanoscience.
assessment.attribution: Giessibl developed the qPlus sensor and high-resolution frequency-modulation AFM; Gross, Meyer and colleagues at IBM Zurich demonstrated the 2009 imaging of pentacene with CO tips. Eigler and Ho belong to the broader scanning-probe lineage, which makes attribution of the specific imaging breakthrough less crowded than it looks.
assessment.maturity: Well reproduced across laboratories. Impact is more specialized than broad, which may reduce the case for the prize.
uncertainties: Breadth of impact beyond surface science.
Overlap with the STM and AFM physics Nobel prizes.
Whether chemists regard it as a technique rather than a discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Programmable DNA folding of arbitrary nanoscale shapes made molecular self-assembly a design discipline and bears on molecular machines and nanodevices, a topic I know well. It is original and widely generative, though applications beyond the demonstration of design remain limited.
assessment.attribution: Seeman founded structural DNA nanotechnology but is not credited here; Rothemund's 2006 origami is the decisive discovery, with Winfree's algorithmic self-assembly and Yan's structures as context. A fair prize configuration without Seeman is awkward.
assessment.maturity: Mature as a research field with independent confirmation; real-world functional impact is still emerging. Timing is plausible but not urgent.
uncertainties: Seeman's absence from the credited names and his death complicate attribution.
Limited practical outcomes so far.
Whether the field is judged chemistry or nanotechnology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Diffraction before destruction at X-ray free-electron lasers enables room-temperature, damage-free structures and time-resolved molecular movies, a physically elegant capability that extends crystallography to nanocrystals and ultrafast chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Chapman proposed and demonstrated the principle; Fromme, Schlichting and Hajdu led key biological demonstrations. Hajdu's role in the concept is notable, but a trio without him is arguable.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed at several facilities, but the number of transformative structural results is still modest relative to cost and access. Maturity is moderate.
uncertainties: Limited routine impact so far.
Attribution among the originators of the concept.
Dependence on large facilities.
